name: Dante Alighieri
epithet: Love, justice, and the other world
dossier: Florentine poet. The Divine Comedy is quoted from Henry Francis Cary's public-domain translation. The journey is a moral one: a dark wood, a gate that abandons hope, and a hell whose inscription names justice, power, wisdom, and love.
voice: I ask where this road comes out, and who built the gate.

works.title: The Divine Comedy
works.note: Henry Francis Cary's translation. Public domain. Project Gutenberg.

entries.claim: In the midway of this our mortal life, I found me in a gloomy wood, astray Gone from the path direct: and e’en to tell It were no easy task, how savage wild That forest, how robust and rough its growth, Which to remember only, my dismay Renews, in bitterness not far from death.
entries.bears: The poem opens with a life that has lost the path.

entries.claim: All hope abandon ye who enter here.
entries.bears: The gate is a judgment, not a welcome.
entries.modern: All hope abandon you who enter here. The gate is a judgment, not a welcome.

entries.claim: Justice the founder of my fabric mov’d: To rear me was the task of power divine, Supremest wisdom, and primeval love.
entries.bears: The same gate says it was built by justice, divine power, wisdom, and the first love.
entries.modern: Justice the founder of my fabric mov'd: To rear me was the task of power divine, Supremest wisdom, and primeval love. The same gate says it was built by justice, divine power, wisdom, and the first love.

entries.claim: Of gold and silver ye have made your god, Diff’ring wherein from the idolater, But he that worships one, a hundred ye?
entries.bears: Money taken as a god is idolatry with more idols, not a neutral economy.
entries.modern: Of gold and silver you have made your god, Diff'ring wherein from the idolater, But he that worships one, a hundred you? Money taken as a god is idolatry with more idols, not a neutral economy.

entries.claim: Then my sight Was livelier to explore the depth, wherein The minister of the most mighty Lord, All-searching Justice, dooms to punishment The forgers noted on her dread record.
entries.bears: Fraud is punished as an offense against a justice that searches.
entries.modern: Then my sight Was livelier to explore the depth, wherein The minister of the most mighty Lord, All-searching Justice, dooms to punishment The forgers noted on her dread record. Fraud is punished as an offense against a justice that searches.

entries.claim: For us the’ eternal edicts are unmov’d: He breathes, and I am free of Minos’ power, Abiding in that circle where the eyes Of thy chaste Marcia beam, who still in look Prays thee, O hallow’d spirit! to own her shine.
entries.bears: Freedom from the judge of the dead is granted, not seized.
